items.title: No Injuries Reported as Fire Crews Extinguish Mississauga Apartment Blaze
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a fire broke out in a Mississauga apartment unit on Sunday, with crews called to the scene before the flames were extinguished. According to police, there are no reports of anyone being physically injured in the fire. The outlet reports Mississauga Fire and Emergency Services remained on scene afterward to investigate what caused the blaze. According to the outlet, several roads in the surrounding area were closed while crews worked, though residents living on Kaneff Crescent still had access to their street. Police are asking members of the public to avoid the area until the scene clears. The outlet reports the cause of the fire had not been released as of Sunday.

items.title: Man Dies After Early-Morning Stabbing, Peel Police Say Attacker Fled Scene
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a man has died after being stabbed in Mississauga in the early hours of Sunday, Oct. 25. According to Peel Regional Police, officers responded to a call reporting the stabbing and found a man who had been stabbed, and he was later pronounced dead from his injuries. The outlet reports the person responsible fled the area before officers arrived, and police currently have no description of a suspect to release. Police say the attack appears to have been an isolated incident rather than part of any broader threat to the public. According to the outlet, a large police presence remained in the area as investigators worked the scene, and nearby residents should expect road closures while the investigation continues. The victim's name has not been released. Police are asking anyone with information to call Peel Regional Police at 905-453-3311 and reference incident number PR260362288.

items.title: Three-Way Toss-Up Headlines Mississauga's Mayoral Race Heading Into Monday's Vote
items.summary: CityNews Toronto reports Mississauga's mayoral race is among the most closely watched in Ontario, with polling suggesting any of the top three candidates could come out on top in Monday's election. According to the outlet, the contest pits Alvin Tedjo against both the city's sitting mayor, Carolyn Parrish, and former mayor Bonnie Crombie, who is attempting a comeback bid for her old job. The outlet reports Crombie left the mayor's chair in 2024 to run for the leadership of the Ontario Liberal Party. According to CityNews, after failing to win a seat in the last provincial election, she formally stepped down as party leader in January 2026. The outlet reports she then entered the Mississauga mayoral race this past July, setting up Monday's three-way contest between her, Parrish and Tedjo.

items.title: Driver Flees After Striking Pedestrian on Mississauga Road Early Sunday
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a pedestrian was taken to hospital after being struck by a vehicle early Sunday morning in Mississauga, with the driver fleeing before officers arrived. According to Peel Regional Police, the collision was reported in the early hours of Oct. 25, and the driver did not remain at the scene afterward. The outlet reports the victim was taken to a local hospital with injuries that are not considered life-threatening. Police say the southbound lanes in the area were closed for the investigation but have since reopened to traffic. According to the outlet, officers have not released a description of the vehicle or the driver involved. Police are asking anyone with information to call Peel Regional Police at 905-453-3311 and ask for 11 Division, or to contact Peel Crime Stoppers anonymously at 1-800-222-TIPS.

items.title: Fibromyalgia Forced Her to Rely on Amazon Deliveries, Then the Company Banned Her Account
items.summary: CTV News reports a Mississauga woman who lives with fibromyalgia found herself locked out of Amazon after the retailer banned her account this past summer. According to the outlet, Sharon Jamison depends on home delivery for her weekly purchases because her condition limits her energy and causes persistent pain, so the ban on her account was more than just an inconvenience. The outlet reports her orders were cancelled over what Amazon described only as unspecified policy violations, and her attempts to fix the problem left her stuck in a loop of chatbots and automated replies. Jamison told CTV News the restriction began after she bought a portable air conditioner, having cancelled an order for the same item earlier, and she suspects that sequence triggered Amazon's fraud detection system. According to the outlet, when CTV News contacted Amazon directly, a spokesperson said the company had fully restored her access, apologized for the error and was reviewing its processes to prevent similar mistakes. The outlet reports Jamison also received a $200 gift card from Amazon for the trouble.

items.title: Most Ontario Voters Will Still Cast a Paper Ballot Monday, Even as Online Options Grow
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports Ontario residents in 414 towns and cities, including Mississauga, head to the polls Monday, Oct. 26, to elect mayors, councillors and school board trustees. According to the outlet, a handful of municipalities skip the vote entirely because their councils are made up of representatives chosen at the lower-tier level rather than elected directly citywide. The outlet reports that while some municipalities have shifted entirely to phone-in or online voting, most Ontario communities still run their elections through traditional paper ballots cast at a polling station. Many of those communities also offer telephone, online or mail-in voting alongside the paper ballot option, according to the outlet. Mississauga.com reports the easiest way for a registered voter to confirm where to go is to check the voter information card mailed to them several weeks before election day, since anyone who voted in a past municipal election is likely already registered.

items.title: Coroner Sets November Date for Inquest Into 2020 Death of Jamal Francique
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a coroner's inquest into the death of Jamal Francique, who died after an interaction with Peel Regional Police in Mississauga nearly seven years ago, will begin next month. According to Dr. Jennifer M. Dmetrichuk, the regional supervising coroner for the Central Region, the inquest is set to open on Thursday, Nov. 12. The outlet reports Francique, 28, died on Jan. 9, 2020, days after the Jan. 7 interaction with officers, and that an inquest into his death is mandatory under Ontario's Coroners Act. According to the outlet, the inquest will examine the circumstances surrounding his death and is expected to last 11 days, hearing from about nine witnesses, with the jury able to make recommendations aimed at preventing future deaths. The outlet reports Bonnie Goldberg will preside over the inquest and Roger Shallow will serve as inquest counsel, with proceedings held by video conference and open for members of the public to watch live online.

items.title: Peel Police Report 20 Per Cent Drop in Vehicle Thefts, Still Call Auto Theft a Top Priority
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say fewer vehicles are being stolen across the region, even as the force continues to treat auto theft as a top enforcement priority. According to police, 4,014 vehicles worth about $178 million were stolen in the 12 months ending in June 2026, down from 5,005 vehicles worth $257 million the year before, a 20 per cent drop in vehicles stolen and a 31 per cent drop in their total value. Police say thefts have fallen by 50 per cent since 2023, and officers laid 1,217 criminal charges tied to auto theft between January 2025 and June 2026. According to police, the force credits the improvement to strong partnerships, shared intelligence and coordinated enforcement, along with continued investment in prevention efforts. Police said in a press release that auto theft and cargo crime do more than steal property, underscoring why the issue remains a key priority even as the numbers improve.
